prediction_question: The lead probed was the ITU DataHub (datahub.itu.int), the ITU's free dissemination channel for its ICT statistics: 'hundreds of ICT indicators' on 'about 200 economies' (connectivity, usage, affordability, price baskets, regulatory information), collected via annual questionnaires to governments. The task family it supports is a next-year country-level change forecast on an ICT indicator panel. Rejected on task shape and mirror grounds: annual country panels (persistence-dominated, positives clustered into a few global trend periods) already republished by the World Bank as a downloadable dataset.
prediction_time: Would have been the end of reference year Y (annual panels; the publisher updates on a questionnaire schedule - the site publishes a consolidated BDT data questionnaire schedule per year) with features from years <= Y. Workable in principle; not the failure.
target_definition: Would have been a binary change target on a country-year ICT indicator (e.g. will the share of individuals using the internet rise next year) - a level target is the measured persistence failure mode. Not reached: the mirror and licence findings close the lead first.

Under the terms of this licence, you may copy, redistribute, and adapt the Data for non-commercial purposes, provided the work is appropriately cited.' Plus third-party-data caveat ('users must refer to the owners' terms of use') and no-endorsement/no-logo terms.

sources.name: World Bank Data 360 / Data Catalog republication of the ITU DataHub (the mirror that already exists in usable form)
sources.api: Anonymous download; the Data 360 indicator pages carry the source's own licence label ('License: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO' on e.g. IT_CEL_SETS mobile-cellular subscriptions, 230 economies, 2000-2024, annual), while the Data Catalog dataset page claims CC BY 4.0 for the same republished copy - conflicting licence labels between the two World Bank channels; the publisher's own instrument (NC-SA) governs.
sources.license: Conflicting republisher labels measured; upstream NC-SA terms carry through regardless.
sources.access: Anonymous; already packaged by a third party as a downloadable dataset.

license_evidence: Measured 2026-10-22 by reading datahub.itu.int/about/ in a real browser (rendered text, quoted verbatim): 'The Data is licensed to the public through a Creative Commons Attribution-Non-Commercial-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO license. Under the terms of this licence, you may copy, redistribute, and adapt the Data for non-commercial purposes, provided the work is appropriately cited.' Attribution + NonCommercial + ShareAlike: the conditions would have to carry through unchanged to any release, and an NC term sits badly on a benchmark intended for (commercial) AI evaluation. Recorded as class B (open but conditional) - not the primary rejection reason.

Plain-client 403 evidence: datahub.itu.int answers 403 (919 B) to curl from the coordinator on five paths probed (2026-10-22); the skill's rule (a 403 to a plain HTTP client is not licence silence) was followed - the page was re-read in a real browser before any terms claim was recorded.

World Bank Data 360 pages label the republished ITU indicators 'License: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO' while the WB Data Catalog copy of the same data claims CC BY 4.0 (both read 2026-10-22 via search) - republisher licence labels conflict; the publisher's own instrument is the NC-SA one.
split_strategy: Not applicable - rejected at discovery. The panel grain (about 200 economies x annual periods, 2000-2024 measured on the WB mirror for IT_CEL_SETS) would have produced three disjoint windows easily, but the positives of any change target cluster into a few global-trend years and the level target is persistence-dominated; and the World Bank already distributes the identical panel as a dataset, so no formulation of ours would be the usable form.

measurements.access_probes_2026_10_22: datahub.itu.org (wrong TLD): connection failure (HTTP 000) from the coordinator. datahub.itu.int: HTTP 403 (919 B) to plain curl on /, /about/, /api/, /indicators/, /data/; loads in a real browser (About page rendered 11,614 chars, licence sentence quoted verbatim). The 403 pattern is a bot wall - the skill's '403 is not silence' rule was applied.
measurements.grain_2026_10_22: Publisher's own scope statement (About page, read in-browser): hundreds of ICT indicators, about 200 economies; collections named are annual questionnaire series (Household ICT Indicators, World Telecommunication Indicators, ICT Price Baskets, Regulatory Information, Tariff Policies). Indicator catalogue years measured on the WB mirror: e.g. mobile-cellular subscriptions IT_CEL_SETS, 230 economies, 2000-2024, updated annual.
measurements.mirror_2026_10_22: The World Bank republishes the ITU DataHub as a downloadable dataset: data360.worldbank.org/en/dataset/ITU_DH (indicator pages with per-indicator licence labels CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO) and datacatalog.worldbank.org dataset 0067055 'ITU Data Hub' (5.6 MB, last updated 2026-03-14, claiming CC BY 4.0 for the copy). The same numbers therefore already exist in a bulk-downloadable form from a second major portal.
measurements.cost_of_this_verdict_2026_10_22: Six plain-client fetches (all 403 or connection failure) + one real-browser page read. No bulk pull, no scratch data.

rejection_reason: Aggregate-panel task shape plus an existing mirror: the DataHub is annual country panels (~200 economies) of questionnaire-collected indicators - a level target is persistence-dominated and a change target's positives cluster into a few global-trend years - and the World Bank already redistributes the identical DataHub as a downloadable dataset (Data 360 dataset ITU_DH / Data Catalog 0067055), so an ML-ready-equivalent distribution channel already exists. The publisher's NC-SA licence (class B) would additionally have to carry through unchanged, further limiting a benchmark's use. Closed rather than parked.
next_action: None - closed on task-shape and mirror grounds. Re-open only if ITU ships a row-level or event-level product (the satellite-filings registry in the Radiocommunication sector is the only such candidate family known; it was not probed this session and may be terms-restricted).
